claims.text: The ability to form and continuously regenerate a stable, adherent passive oxide film under sliding contact governs an HEA's resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
HEAs containing more robust film-forming elements sustain lower tribocorrosion loss by preventing metal contact and limiting anodic dissolution.
The two proposed equiatomic HEAs have equal hardness of approximately 4 GPa.
Equiatomic Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni is expected to form strong Al/Ti-rich oxides.
Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni lacks the strong Al/Ti-driven film-forming capability attributed to Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni.
The controlled comparison uses reciprocating sliding in 0.1 M NaCl at pH 7 and 25 degrees C under a 1 N load, 10 mm/s speed, and 5000 cycles.
The relevant structural mediator is continuous formation and repair of the passive oxide layer within the wear track.
After mechanical removal of its film, Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni rapidly repassivates.
Rapid repassivation sustains a protective barrier that lowers friction, limits fresh-metal exposure, and reduces anodic current.
Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni replenishes its passive film less effectively and therefore exhibits greater corrosion-wear synergy.
Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni will exhibit approximately 50% lower combined material loss than Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni under the specified test conditions.
Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni will exhibit approximately 40% lower steady-state corrosion current under sliding than Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
For Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni, combined tribocorrosion loss will be less than the sum of isolated wear and isolated corrosion losses, indicating antagonistic interaction.
The protective effect will diminish above approximately 5 N because repassivation can no longer offset mechanically induced film removal.
The protective effect will diminish outside pH 6-8 where repassivation kinetics are expected to slow drastically.
A 30-70% reduction in combined loss is estimated based on oxide kinetics.
The magnitude of the effect may vary with solution chemistry and microstructural state.
Equal or greater combined loss or corrosion current for Al-Ti-Cr-Fe-Ni relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
Combined loss exceeding the sum of isolated wear and corrosion losses by more than 10% would falsify the hypothesis.
